problem:
Consider the function $f(x,y)=-x(y-1)^{2}.$ What are the missing entries in the following sign table of $f(x,y)?$

| $y>1$ |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<1$ |  |  |
|  | $x<0$ | $x>0$ |

feedback.problem:
Consider the function $f(x,y)=-{x}^{2}(y-2).$ Fill in the missing signs in the sign table of $f(x,y)$ shown below.

| $y>2$ | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<2$ | {{field-3}} | {{field-4}} |
|  | $x<0$ | $x>0$ |
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=0$ and $y=2.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14037232/assets/be201671c4862874082f9aa2bf598a19a629d808e263ac410629229bb97c8ebf.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14037232/assets/dc763b1ceba087be22a05c0e0f411d82e1a6ae13566f9c9625fa2e164d8be1ce.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $-{x}^{2}$ | $(y-2)$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-Left | $(-1,3)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Top-Right | $(1,3)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(-1,1)$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(1,1)$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |

 

Using the *last* column of the table above, we get the following picture:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14037232/assets/5b2e7277212bacfb039b94783de1a669de6aed764ac8584c23f253448d4fc517.png)

Finally, we fill in the required sign table.

| $y>2$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<2$ | $+$ | $+$ |
|  | $x<0$ | $x>0$ |
